name: Row 1, Section 1, Scene 1
background: Two kings, Dharmaketu (the father) and Chandraketu (the son), stood on a chariot with Lokeswor. In front of them, the Amoghapash Buddha rode his divine mount: a peacock.
note: Interpreted from iconography due to damaged inscriptions on this scene

name: Row 1, Section 1, Scene 2
background: On the day of Shukla Ashtami, the two kings made a religious circle for Shree Amoghapash Lokeshwor and worshipped him. As a result of their devotion, it rained.

name: Row 1, Section 1, Scene 3
background: A great sage then began reciting the Shukla Ashtami story of Shree Amoghapash Lokeshwor to the two kings, Dharmaketu and Chandraketu.

name: Row 1, Section 1, Scene 4
background: The great sage told stories of Shree Amoghapash Lokeshwor’s compassion and explained how the two kings could also reach heaven.

name: Row 1, Section 2, Scene 1
background: Suddenly, the father and son stood on their chariots and began fighting each other.

name: Row 1, Section 2, Scene 2
background: There had been no rainfall in Magadha for a long time, and people hadn’t had anything to eat. So they fought against each other and killed their own family and relatives. The dogs and crows ate the dead bodies.

name: Row 1, Section 2, Scene 3
background: All the water fountains and ponds in Magadha were dry.

name: Row 1, Section 2, Scene 4
background: But seeing their country’s ponds full of water again, both kings of Magadha were surprised and confused about how such a miracle had occurred.

name: Row 2, Section 1, Scene 1
background: All of the deities and devotees came to Bungamati to see Lokeshwor.
note: Interpreted from iconography due to damaged inscriptions on this scene

name: Row 2, Section 1, Scene 2
background: Among them were Amitabh Buddha, Mahadev, Brahma, Vishnu, Vajrapani, Krakuchanda Tathagata Buddha, …

name: Row 2, Section 1, Scene 3
background: …household monks, household nuns, and other vajra or diamond beings.

name: Row 2, Section 1, Scene 4
background: A religious procession for Trailokenath was held by hoisting many flags and ritual cloths and by dropping various sweet dishes, such as yomari and coconut, from the top of the chariot.
note: This scene shows the upper half of Bunga Dyo’s chariot and belongs with the rest of scene 19 in the third register, but it appears in the second register, breaking the line of inscriptions that crowns the third register

name: Row 2, Section 1, Scene 5
background: The household monks and house nuns sat to perform khatkarma, the six actions of purification.

name: Row 2, Section 2, Scene 1
background: But instead of performing khatkarma, the household monk left his first wife and committed immoral acts. So Yamdoot, the agent of the god of death, beat them on the chest with a hammer and tied them with snakes to punish them.

name: Row 2, Section 2, Scene 2
background: Because of his immoral actions, the household monk had to endure pain and suffering.

name: Row 2, Section 2, Scene 3
background: Then all the gods gathered at the Nirmal Tirtha, the sacred water site.

name: Row 3, Section 1, Scene 1
background: The idol and temple of Trailokyanath were ordered to be restored and cleaned before the deity’s consecration.

name: Row 3, Section 1, Scene 2
background: The Vajracharya priests and the royal family were ready to perform the ritual.

name: Row 3, Section 1, Scene 3
background: On Sambat 832, on the day of Shrawan Chaturdashi, Wednesday, Shree Trailokyanath sat in the chariot. This was done in the presence of Jaswantaju, Maheshwarju, Kayashtha Vishnu Vir, and King Mahindra Malla Dev Thakur.
note: The list of names was visible on its own line within the painting’s scene, rather than on the line of inscription over the third register.

name: Row 3, Section 1, Scene 4
background: A religious procession for Trailokyanath was held by hoisting many flags and ritual cloths and by dropping various sweet dishes, such as yomari and coconut, from the top of the chariot. Minnath’s chariot also followed during the festival.
note: This is the second part of what we saw in scene 12

name: Row 3, Section 2, Scene 1
background: During the ritual process, an Acharya priest set up various kalash, or vessels. He then performed ritual worship, reciting sacred texts and offering to a ritual fire. Shree Trailoknath then underwent the ten essential religious rites of life in the Hindu tradition, known as Dashakarma, including rites for birth, marriage, and death.

name: Row 3, Section 2, Scene 2
background: He was then bathed in Shree Ganga water, worshiped by blowing a conch shell filled with water from 4 different oceans, and bathed from a silver Kalash with a mixture of 5 sacred ingredients called Panchamrit.

name: Row 3, Section 2, Scene 3
background: Playing various musical instruments, including animal-horn instruments, burning fragrant incense, and ringing ritual bells, Shree Trailoknath was taken for the great ablution.
